# SmallDivisorPulse — every small number divides a speed of any counterexample

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: proved in source file · **Diagram:** [The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves](../../GRAPH.md#the-lonely-runner-pile-ups-shifts-and-residue-sieves)

Normalize so the runner to be lonely stands still and the others have whole-number speeds. If no speed is divisible by some number from 2 up to the field size, then at the time one over that number every moving runner is at least one over that number from the start, which is enough. So in any set of speeds that is never lonely, every number from 2 up to the field size divides some speed, and their least common multiple divides the product of the speeds. Rosenfeld 2025, Lemma 4. The general form of the even/odd pulse.
